T01_spike_frame_isolation.title: Spike visual iframe isolation in Electron and write the design
T01_spike_frame_isolation.instruction: Goal: prove the isolation model on the real app before anything is built, then write the design that later nodes follow. Steps: 1. Read the files named in context, plus docs/DESIGN.md (untrusted content, CSP and protocol, Markdown and prompt). 2. Write a small throwaway harness, deleted afterwards or kept documented under scripts/. Measure each of these: a. A srcdoc, data: or blob: iframe inside the app://pigna page inherits the parent CSP (script-src 'self'), so inline scripts in it are blocked. Confirm this, because it is the reason for a dedicated scheme. b. A privileged custom scheme (proposed name `pigna-visual`) serves a frame document with its own CSP header. The parent CSP only needs `frame-src pigna-visual:`. Find the minimal registerSchemesAsPrivileged flags. c. In an iframe with sandbox="allow-scripts", the origin is opaque. fetch, XHR, WebSocket, remote //@import/font, window.open, top navigation, form submit and alert() are all blocked or no-ops. The parent page and window.studio are unreachable. d. postMessage between parent and frame works. Validating `event.source === iframe.contentWindow` is the right check. e. A `while(true){}` in the frame does or does not freeze the transcript. That depends on whether Electron isolates sandboxed iframes out of process. Find the mitigation if it freezes, for example a frame watchdog that removes the frame after N seconds without a heartbeat. f. prefers-color-scheme follows nativeTheme inside the frame. 3. Add a 'Visuals' section to docs/DESIGN.md that fixes: - the fence contract: the tag `visual`, fragment only, a 64 KB cap, and behavior when the setting is off; - the scheme name and frame CSP; - the postMessage protocol, with message types such as render, tokens, height, open-link and error; - the hydration lifecycle while streaming and after it ends; - the size and height limits; - the freeze mitigation. Deliverables: the DESIGN.md section, plus a node report with the measured results for a-f. Acceptance: every claim in the design is backed by a measurement from step 2. No production code is changed yet, apart from optional harness files.
T01_spike_frame_isolation.context:
Feature: optional inline HTML visuals in assistant replies, like the Codex app's inline visualizations and Claude's inline visuals, toggled in pi-gna's Settings.
Contract: the agent writes a fenced block tagged `visual` holding an HTML fragment (not a full page). The Markdown prose around it must answer the question by itself; the visual only supplements it. pi-gna renders the fragment in a sandboxed iframe (sandbox="allow-scripts", no allow-same-origin) served from a dedicated scheme with its own CSP: no network at all, no navigation, no popups, no forms. The iframe loads a bundled visual kit: pi-gna's theme tokens plus a small component vocabulary, so fragments look native and the agent writes structure, not styling.
Why not copy Codex: Codex has the agent write a fragment file under ~/.codex/visualizations/<date>/<thread>/ and emit `::codex-inline-vis{file=...}`. That fails silently on path mismatches (openai/codex#32054) and its frame CSP allows scripts from unpkg/jsdelivr/esm.sh. Inline fences keep the visual in the session JSONL, so it survives resume and history, and the frame needs no network.
Key files: src/renderer/src/lib/markdown.ts (marked + DOMPurify), src/renderer/src/components/Markdown.tsx (hydration and click delegation), src/main/app-protocol.ts (renderer CSP: frame-src 'none' today) and src/renderer/index.html (dev meta CSP), src/shared/settings.ts plus src/main/settings.ts and components/Settings.tsx (wallpaperLoop is the boolean-toggle pattern), src/main/session-host.ts (piArgs appends resources/pigna-prompt.md via --append-system-prompt), src/renderer/src/styles.css (theme tokens --canvas --panel --fg --muted --faint --accent --ok --bad --warn --line, light mode via prefers-color-scheme), docs/DESIGN.md (architecture and CDP test recipes), scripts/fake-pi.mjs and scripts/cdp.mjs (UI verification).
Tests: vitest (pnpm test), node environment only, no jsdom. CI runs pnpm typecheck, pnpm test and pnpm build.
T01_spike_frame_isolation.report:
## Outcome
Isolation model proven on Electron 44.5.1. `docs/DESIGN.md` has a new "Visuals" section (fence contract, scheme and CSP, postMessage protocol, hydration, limits, freeze mitigation). The harness is kept as `scripts/visual-isolation-spike.mjs`.

## Facts Learned (measured)
- a. srcdoc, data: and blob: iframes in app://pigna load, but their inline scripts do not run. A control with a parent CSP allowing 'unsafe-inline' does run them. A dedicated scheme is therefore required.
- b. pigna-visual with its own CSP header works with only `frame-src pigna-visual:` on the parent. With `frame-src 'none'` it fails with ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CSP. Minimal flags are `{standard:true, secure:true}`. With no flags or `secure` only, the frame loads, but relative URLs and `script-src 'self'` do not work (the kit failed to load).
- c. Origin is "null". fetch, XHR, WebSocket, remote img/link, localStorage, top.location, top.document and parent.studio are all blocked. alert returns undefined, window.open returns null, form.submit is blocked by CSP, and target=_blank opens nothing. Clicking an `<a href>` navigates the frame itself to a CSP error page and destroys it, so the shell must preventDefault clicks and post open-link.
- d. postMessage works both ways. event.origin is "null". `event.source === iframe.contentWindow` is the correct check: true for the frame, false for a self-posted spoof.
- e. `for(;;){}` does not freeze the parent. The frame runs in its own process (osProcessId differs); parent timers ran 50/50 with a worst gap of 21 ms. Removing the iframe does not stop the loop, and a later frame on the same host did not load. A different host loaded normally, and SIGKILL of frame.osProcessId from main stops the loop. Design: one host per frame, a heartbeat watchdog, and a kill from main.
- f. A live nativeTheme flip fires matchMedia change in the frame. A frame loaded under light reports light. The hidden spike window sometimes reported light for a frame loaded right after switching back to dark (timing). Re-verify in the visible app via CDP_SCHEME.
- g. A ResizeObserver in the frame delivers the height (334 for a 300 px block plus margins).
- The spike prints "Check failed ... site_info.cc IsValid" lines on stderr (Chromium noise with the custom scheme and opaque origin). They are harmless but appeared in every run.

## Decisions Made
Scheme `pigna-visual`, one random host per frame, fragment delivered via a `render` message (not the URL), 64 KB fragment cap, 480 px max height, 8 frames max, 5 s ready and heartbeat timeouts, unclosed fences stay a placeholder while streaming, and fallback to a plain code block.

## Files Touched
docs/DESIGN.md, scripts/visual-isolation-spike.mjs (new). No production code.

## Interfaces Changed
None (designed only: renderer CSP `frame-src pigna-visual:`, a visual-kill IPC, and the postMessage protocol).

## Verification
`node_modules/.bin/electron scripts/visual-isolation-spike.mjs` was run repeatedly and prints the JSON report. `pnpm typecheck` passes. Committed 072ca5c.

## Risks
- The 5 s watchdog and 8-frame limits are chosen values, not measured.
- Kill-on-unmount and the heartbeat-driven watchdog are designed but not exercised end to end. The spike only measured SIGKILL of a spinning frame's osProcessId.
- Theme-on-load flakiness is untested in a visible window.
- The DESIGN claim that `render` re-creates scripts so they run is not measured.

## Recommended Next Step
Implement the scheme handler, CSP change and Settings toggle, then the frame shell and kit, then the Markdown hydration. Verify the watchdog and theme with fake-pi and CDP in the real app.

T03_visual_scheme_main.title: Serve the visual frame from a sandboxed scheme with its own CSP
T03_visual_scheme_main.instruction:
Goal: implement the main-process side of the isolation design from T01_spike_frame_isolation.

Steps:
1. Register the frame scheme (name and privileges from the DESIGN.md Visuals section) next to registerAppScheme in src/main/app-protocol.ts, or in a new src/main/visual-protocol.ts.
2. Serve exactly the bundled frame assets: the runtime HTML, JS and CSS that T04 builds. Put them under resources/visual/ or wherever the design says. Refuse every other path, including traversal.
3. Attach the frame CSP header. As a baseline, adjusted only to what T01 measured:
   `default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data: blob:; font-src data:; media-src data: blob:; connect-src 'none'; frame-src 'none'; object-src 'none'; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none'`
4. Relax only `frame-src` in the renderer CSP, in both src/main/app-protocol.ts and src/renderer/index.html, to allow the frame scheme.
5. Make sure navigation away from the frame and popups stay refused. Check will-frame-navigate and the existing setWindowOpenHandler and will-navigate handlers.
6. Make the assets ship in the packaged app. Check the electron-builder.yml asarUnpack rules if they are read from disk.
7. Add unit tests for the path guard and the CSP strings.

Acceptance:
- pnpm typecheck, pnpm test and pnpm build pass.
- In the dev app, an iframe pointed at the scheme loads.
- The DevTools console shows CSP blocking a fetch from inside it.

T03_visual_scheme_main.report:
## Outcome
pigna-visual scheme is served from main with its own CSP; renderer CSP allows it as frame-src; subframe navigation outside the scheme is refused.
## Facts Learned
- registerSchemesAsPrivileged replaces earlier calls, so both schemes (app, pigna-visual) are registered in one call in registerAppScheme.
- In the running dev app, an iframe sandbox=allow-scripts at pigna-visual://abcd1234ef/doc loads (confirmed via main framesInSubtree) and a fetch('https://example.com') executed inside it is blocked.
- Packaging needs no change: resources/** is already in files and asarUnpack; assets read via onDisk("resources","visual").
## Decisions Made
- Assets: resources/visual/doc.html, kit.css, kit.js; URL map /doc, /kit.css, /kit.js; host must match [a-z0-9-]{8,64}. Anything else 404. Responses are no-store.
- CSP is exactly the baseline (no frame-ancestors, since dev parent is http://localhost).
- will-frame-navigate on the window: non-main frames may only navigate to pigna-visual://. Existing setWindowOpenHandler/will-navigate untouched (popups still denied, main frame still guarded).
- serveVisual() runs in dev and prod.
## Files Touched
src/main/visual-frame.ts (pure: VISUAL_SCHEME, VISUAL_CSP, visualAsset), src/main/visual-frame.test.ts, src/main/visual-protocol.ts (serveVisual), src/main/app-protocol.ts, src/main/index.ts, src/renderer/index.html, resources/visual/{doc.html,kit.css,kit.js}.
## Interfaces Changed
Renderer CSP frame-src 'none' -> pigna-visual: (header and dev meta). Scheme pigna-visual://<id>/{doc,kit.css,kit.js}.
## Verification
pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm build all pass. Dev app run over CDP: frame loaded, fetch blocked from inside. Unit tests cover the path guard and CSP strings. Packaged build not run.
## Risks
- resources/visual/* are placeholders: the next node (frame shell/kit) must replace them (doc.html must load /kit.css and /kit.js).
- Console CSP message was verified as a rejected fetch, not by reading DevTools.
- The 404 response carries no CSP header (harmless, no content).
## Recommended Next Step
Build the real shell and kit into resources/visual/ and add the visual-kill IPC.

T04_visual_kit_runtime.report:
## Outcome
Frame runtime (resources/visual/kit.js), kit CSS (kit.css, 5.5 KB), shell doc (doc.html, container now `#visual`) and a gallery (gallery.html, `?theme=light|dark`) written. Gallery checked in a browser in both themes.

## Files Touched

## Interfaces Changed
doc.html container id root -> visual. Messages: frame->parent ready/height{px}/open-link{href}/error{message}/heartbeat; parent->frame render{html,tokens|vars}/tokens/ping.
## Verification
pnpm typecheck and pnpm test pass. Gallery viewed in light and dark.
## Risks
Not tested in the real frame (CSP, theme-on-load). Callout variants share the accent-soft background. No unit tests for kit.js.
## Recommended Next Step
Build the renderer frame shell and verify with CDP in the real app, including the gallery fragment rendered through render.

T06_visual_block_component.title: Hydrate visual placeholders into sandboxed frames in the transcript
T06_visual_block_component.instruction:
Goal: render visuals in assistant replies in Transcript.tsx when the setting is on.

Steps:
1. Give Markdown.tsx a `visuals` prop, passed only by assistant messages in Transcript.tsx. Activity, ATP, Laments, GitHub and Update stay off for now. Read the live setting from the app store, so toggling off immediately falls back to code blocks.
2. While streaming, render a compact 'Drawing visual…' placeholder for a visual fence instead of dumping raw source. Hydrate once streaming ends, mirroring highlightWithin.
3. Write a VisualFrame component, either in Markdown.tsx or its own file.
   - Mounting: mount it into each placeholder (createRoot or a portal). Create an <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" referrerpolicy="no-referrer" src="<frame scheme URL>">, and send {render, html, tokens} after load. The tokens are read from getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).
   - Messages: accept messages only when event.source === this iframe's contentWindow.
   - Height: size from the height messages, clamped (for example 40 to 560 px), with an 'Expand' toggle beyond the clamp.
   - Theme: re-send tokens when prefers-color-scheme changes.
   - Links: on open-link, call window.studio.openExternal only for http and https URLs.
   - Errors: on error, or on watchdog timeout, show a small inline error with the source.
   - Header: a slim header with the label 'visual', a 'Source' toggle that shows the fragment through the existing code-block highlighting, and Copy.
4. Memoise by fragment source, so a transcript re-render does not reload frames. Unmount frames cleanly.
5. Add styles in styles.css for .visual and its header, matching .code-block.

Acceptance:
- pnpm typecheck, pnpm test and pnpm build pass.
- In the dev app with a fake-pi reply containing a visual, it renders, auto-sizes, follows the theme switch, and falls back to a code block when the setting is turned off.

T06_visual_block_component.report:
## Outcome
Assistant text blocks render ```visual fences as sandboxed pigna-visual iframes (VisualFrame) when Settings.visuals is on; off falls back to normal code blocks. Not exercised in the live dev app (no CDP/fake-pi run).
## Facts Learned
Markdown only gets closed-fence placeholders from markdown.ts; unclosed streaming fences are rewritten in Markdown.tsx to "*Drawing visual…*" via regex before parsing.
## Decisions Made
Markdown gets `visuals` prop AND reads useApp settings.visuals (both required). While streaming, placeholders show "Drawing visual…" and hydrate after streaming ends via createRoot per placeholder (unmounted in setTimeout on cleanup). Frame id random 16 hex per VisualFrame; height clamp 40-560 with Expand/Collapse; watchdog 8s without any frame message (frame heartbeats 1/s); theme change re-sends tokens via matchMedia; open-link only http(s). T07_visual_prompt.title: Write the visuals prompt and append it only when the setting is on
T07_visual_prompt.instruction:
Goal: teach agents when and how to use visuals, so they help and do not produce slop.

Steps:
1. Create resources/pigna-visual-prompt.md, kept short (under ~60 lines). Cover:
   - Contract: a ```visual fence holding an HTML fragment that uses the kit classes (list them with one-line meanings and one small example). Inline <svg> and a short <script> are allowed for interaction. There is no network, so no CDN, fonts, images by URL or fetch. Do not set colors or fonts, and use only the kit tokens and classes. Do not include <html>, <head> or <body>.
   - When to use it: structure that prose or a table cannot show well, such as architecture or data flow, state machines, sequences and timelines, quantitative comparisons, option trade-offs with several dimensions, and progress across many items. Interaction only when it reveals something, such as a slider over a parameter.
   - When not to use it: short or conversational answers, anything a Markdown table or list already shows, code (use code fences), decoration, summaries of what you just did, or more than one visual per reply unless asked.
   - Prose-first: the Markdown text must fully answer by itself. The visual adds understanding and never carries the only copy of a fact. Introduce it in one sentence and do not narrate it afterwards.
   - Anti-slop rules:
     - no hero banners, titles restating the question, emoji, gradients, drop shadows, glassmorphism or marketing tone;
     - no filler 'Key insights' cards;
     - label data directly;
     - stay compact (aim under ~150 lines and under 20 KB);
     - use real values from the work, not invented numbers.
2. Update resources/pigna-prompt.md: keep 'raw HTML does not render' for normal Markdown, and point to the visuals section only when it is present. Don't mention visuals at all when it is off.
3. In src/main/session-host.ts piArgs, append `--append-system-prompt <pigna-visual-prompt.md>` when features.visuals is on, for all chat kinds including ATP workers and orchestrators. Make sure the file ships unpacked (electron-builder.yml).
4. Add a test in the session-host tests, or create a small one, asserting the arg appears only when visuals is on.

Acceptance: pnpm typecheck and pnpm test pass. With the setting on, a new chat's pi args include the visual prompt, and with it off they do not.

T08_fixtures_cdp_verification.title: Verify visuals end to end with fake-pi fixtures and CDP, including hostile fragments
T08_fixtures_cdp_verification.instruction: Goal: prove the feature works and is contained, on the real app surface. Steps: 1. Extend scripts/fake-pi.mjs, or add fixtures, with replies containing: - a good architecture diagram (steps plus svg); - a comparison (bars plus a table); - an interactive slider; - two visuals in one reply; - a streamed visual split across chunks; - an oversized fragment over 64 KB; - hostile fragments: fetch to a local http server, , top.location change, window.open, form submit, alert, an access attempt on parent.studio, a link to javascript:, and a `while(true){}` loop. 2. Using scripts/cdp.mjs against a test instance (PIGNA_BACKGROUND=1, PIGNA_CWD), as described in docs/DESIGN.md, check: - The good visuals render and auto-size, with screenshots in light and dark. - The streaming placeholder appears and is then hydrated. - The local http server receives zero requests from the hostile fragments. - The app does not navigate, and no window opens. - The transcript stays responsive under the infinite loop, and the watchdog or error UI appears. - Toggling the setting off turns visuals into code blocks live. 3. Fix any defect found in the owning code, and add regression unit tests where it is testable. 4. Add the verification recipe to docs/DESIGN.md next to the existing CDP recipes. Deliverables: the fixtures, any fixes, the recipe, and screenshots referenced in the node report (kept out of git unless the repo already keeps such assets). Acceptance: every check above passes, with evidence in the report.

T08_fixtures_cdp_verification.report:
## Outcome
Visuals verified end to end in a real test instance (fake-pi + CDP). Three defects found and fixed. Screenshots (not in git): /tmp/vis/shots/{architecture-light,architecture-dark,comparison-light,comparison-dark,hostile,loop-error}.png.
## Facts Learned
- All checks passed after fixes: architecture renders (106px) and comparison (170px) in light and dark; two visuals in one reply render in separate renderer processes; the slider works (input 11 -> #out "11"); streamed fixture shows "Drawing visual…" then hydrates to an iframe; 70 KB fragment shows the "too large" note + code block, no frame.
- Hostile fixture (9 fences): counting server saw 0 requests from the fragments; app location unchanged; only 1 window / webContents; parent.studio access from the frame = "blocked"; alert is a no-op; javascript: link opens nothing. A click on the http link calls openExternal (by design; the only request seen came from that click, since window.studio is frozen and cannot be stubbed).
- `while(true){}`: page timer kept ticking (30 ticks/3 s, max gap 103 ms); watchdog showed "Visual stopped responding" after ~8 s.
- Toggling Settings > Agent > Inline visuals off turns the visuals into `visual` code blocks live and drops frame processes; on restores frames.
## Decisions Made
- Defect 1 (Markdown.tsx): the streaming placeholder wiped the hidden `.visual-src`, so when streaming ended with unchanged html the frame got an empty source (blank 40px frame). Now the source is kept and a "Drawing visual…" span is appended; `pending` class removed on hydration.
- Defect 2 (VisualFrame/kit.js): the frame can load before the parent effect listens, losing its `ready`. Frame now acks `rendered`; parent re-sends render on heartbeats until acked.
- Defect 3: DESIGN.md's visual-kill was never implemented, so a looping frame kept a core at 99% after the error UI. Added IPC `visualKill` / `window.studio.killVisual(frameId)`, main kills the process via pure `visualFrameToKill` (id validated, never the app window pid); called on error and on unmount. Verified the loop process is gone afterwards.
## Files Touched
scripts/fake-pi.mjs (FAKE_FIXTURE, FAKE_CHUNK), scripts/fake-pi-visuals.mjs (new), scripts/cdp-frame.mjs (new, eval inside a visual frame), docs/DESIGN.md (recipe "Verifying inline visuals"), resources/visual/kit.js, src/renderer/src/components/{Markdown,VisualFrame}.tsx, src/main/{index,visual-frame,visual-frame.test}.ts, src/preload/index.ts, src/shared/ipc.ts
## Interfaces Changed
`StudioApi.killVisual(frameId)`, IPC `studio:visual-kill`, frame->parent message `rendered`, `visualFrameToKill()` in main/visual-frame.ts.
## Verification
pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm build pass (new unit tests for visualFrameToKill). Live checks above via scripts/cdp.mjs, scripts/cdp-frame.mjs on a /tmp build.
## Risks
Defects 1 and 2 have no unit tests (components untestable in node-only vitest). Watchdog is 8 s, DESIGN.md still says 5 s. Killing on unmount assumes one process per frame (observed: distinct pids for two frames).
## Recommended Next Step
Fix the DESIGN.md watchdog wording if desired; proceed with remaining nodes.

T09_quality_eval_real_agents.title: Evaluate visual quality with real agents and tune the prompt and kit
T09_quality_eval_real_agents.instruction:
Goal: check with real models that agents use visuals when they help and skip them otherwise, and that the visuals do not look like slop.

Steps:
1. Write ~10 eval prompts in docs/visual-evals.md (or a scripts fixture). Mix them like this:
   - 5 where a visual should help: explain this repo's session-host spawn flow, compare three caching strategies on four dimensions, show the timeline of a failed ATP plan, show test coverage per module from real numbers, and a state machine of a chat's lifecycle;
   - 5 where it should not: a one-line factual question, 'fix this typo', a code snippet request, a yes/no design question, and a summary of an edit just made.
2. Run them in pi-gna with the setting on, on at least two models (for example the current Claude Sonnet and GPT defaults from TASK_DEFAULTS). Capture screenshots.
3. Score each against a rubric:
   - Was a visual used when warranted, and absent when not?
   - Does the prose stand alone?
   - Does it use only kit classes and tokens, with no invented styling?
   - Does it carry no decorative or filler content?
   - Are the data real?
   - Is it legible in both themes?
   - Size in KB.
4. Tune resources/pigna-visual-prompt.md and the kit CSS where the failures cluster. Re-run the failing cases.
5. Record the rubric results before and after in the doc.

Acceptance: at least 4 of the 5 'should' cases use a sensible visual, at most 1 of the 5 'should not' cases does, and no case uses styling outside the kit or network resources.

## Outcome
Eval harness built and run on two real models (claude-bridge/claude-sonnet-5-5, openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol) via `pi -p` with both pi-gna prompts appended.
